analysis:
Both supplied units are BASE text of SSDPrefixCacheTests.swift, a test-only file (base lines 1189-2413). The changed ranges (base 3444-3499, head 3444-3545 and 3685-3727) lie outside the visible lines, so I could not examine the PR's actual diff. The patch excerpt is truncated: it shows only the write-behind big-donation test being refactored into a shared productionWriteBehind helper with productionQueuedByteCap. Nothing in the excerpt touches production source.

The visible base tests cover T-041 mitigations: epoch retention on eviction, TTL sweep and corrupt-block drop; epoch rotation on binding change with a disowned superseded cache that refuses unlinks; symlink-replacement handling without following the link; TTL telemetry counting only owned removals; the write cap; the disk-free reserve; and ready-receipt gating. These show the intended invariants (no cross-root unlink after disownment, no-follow I/O, no ready receipt on corruption or low disk). Because they are test-only and the visible text is unchanged base, no security regression is evident, and no production control is weakened by what I could see.

Remaining questions: the head-side tests at 3467-3545 and 3685-3727 were not supplied. I cannot confirm that the refactor preserves its assertions, namely that oversize donations are dropped rather than stalled and that the production queue bounds are used. Whether the matching production change, such as epoch-rotation removal in SSDPrefixCache, SSDBlockStore or SSDWriteBehind, is in another batch is also unknown. The next pass should check that the tests still assert the production bounds and that the epoch is not a purge primitive, per the T-041 note.
